summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with left-sided chest pain radiating to the abdomen and back, associated with shortness of breath, nausea, and dizziness. Initial evaluation revealed a supratherapeutic INR of 4.3 and severe iron deficiency anemia with a hemoglobin of 7.8 g/dL. A CTA showed an infrarenal aortic ulceration, managed conservatively with INR correction and blood pressure control. She underwent upper endoscopy and colonoscopy, which identified gastritis and diverticulosis as likely sources of occult gastrointestinal bleeding, though no active bleeding was seen. She received two units of packed red blood cells and was started on iron supplementation. Her chest pain was determined to be musculoskeletal, and her hypoxia, likely due to atelectasis and heart strain, improved with diuresis; however, she was discharged on 2 liters of oxygen with exertion. She was stabilized on adjusted warfarin, continued heart failure and GERD medications, and provided with discharge instructions including follow-up for INR monitoring and iron repletion.
